lead_headline: Restaurant tracker explodes with 6 same-day leads—Paperboy Austin import debuts in Highland, Black Rock Coffee adds 13th Denver shop, The Barn finally opens Englewood

restaurant.blurb: 6 leads added today push active count to 61 (31 openings, 30 closures)—highest single-day lead volume since tracker inception. Today's triple-header: Paperboy Denver (Austin brunch's first Texas exit, West Highland), Black Rock Coffee Bar (Oregon chain's 13th Denver, Overland), The Barn South Broadway (Englewood American restaurant after multi-month delays). Yesterday: Snarf's Sandwiches opens Belmar, Wash Park Social replaces defunct Grille. Weekend cluster: Union Station corridor adds Mendocino Farms Highland, Otra Vez Cantina post-pandemic relaunch (CBD), Bad Rabbit Coffee RiNo debut. Closure side: Riot House nightclub shutters December (Union Station, 2-year run), China Jade Seafood exits Federal Boulevard after 15+ years (Westwood). Geographic saturation: Union Station logs 8 leads this week across all concepts, Highland/West Highland captures 4 openings. Lead confidence averages 9.2/10—opening dominance flips last week's parity.

foreclosure.blurb: 42 filings this week—still up 40% from prior week's 30—sustain March's accelerating volatility as 104 auctions queue next seven days. $71M aggregate exposure dominated by single $57M Arapahoe outlier (2038 S Vaughn commercial case) masks underlying residential compression: next-largest filing drops to $795K (Weld County). County standings unchanged: El Paso leads 475 active cases, Arapahoe 451, Weld 435. Two-week pattern crystallizes: filing surges alternate with sub-40 weeks as predictable January rhythm (steady 50+ baseline) gives way to boom-bust cadence. 30 sold, 112 continued this cycle suggest auction clearance rates stabilizing around 27%—backlog accumulation slows but distress pipeline refills faster than Q1 pace. Watch April for seasonal acceleration.

reputation.blurb: 3 mentions yesterday hold 7-day total at 46 (vs prior week's 41, +12%)—third consecutive week above 40-mention threshold. Denver Post remains dominant with 21 pickups (46% share), Instagram delivers 7, Hoodline contributes 5. Notable recent coverage: Hoodline's Colorado THC drink federal regulatory story, Threads' Burnham Yard traffic/parking analysis, Facebook's Denver REIT IPO valuation circulation. Source concentration intensifies: Post plus social platforms command 70% of volume—dual-outlet dependency persists as structural risk, niche publishers (Threads debut, continued Hoodline engagement) provide sporadic diversification. Discovery remains 100% Google News RSS. Monthly pace: 137 mentions through 24 days projects 178-mention March if sustained, tracking 35% above February benchmark—strongest monthly performance year-to-date barring late-month collapse.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +5 yesterday (7 new, 2 canceled) lifts MTD to +39 (+1.7/day), 90-day cumulative to +108 (+1.2/day). Yesterday's acquisition surge—strongest single-day gain since March 16's +4—breaks three-day weekend flat streak. Seven-day window: +16 net (24 new, 8 canceled) slightly trails prior week's +19 but maintains March's elevated 1.7/day rhythm, running 31% above YTD's 1.3/day baseline. Recent two-week pattern: acquisition stabilizes at 3.4/day average (down from early-month 4+ spikes), cancellation floor compresses to 1.1/day (vs March average 1.6/day)—improved retention offsets modest new-subscriber deceleration. March tracking toward 50-55 net monthly gain if pace holds through month-end, potentially strongest monthly performance year-to-date.
